title: WHITE CLAW — SUNSET ROOFTOP
lessons: The player sees White Claw Zero Proof and realizes the brand now offers a 0% alcohol product with familiar social styling.
The player already knows White Claw and sees ClawTails, a line built around recognizable cocktail flavor names.

text: The player sees White Claw Zero Proof and realizes the brand now offers a 0% alcohol product with familiar social styling.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: A White Claw with no alcohol is a funny sentence.

entry-first-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: It still fits in the cooler.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: But the entire point used to be hard seltzer.

entry-first-4.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Zero Proof is 0% alc./vol. The social shorthand can stay even when alcohol is not the job.

choice-first.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I like having the same kind of drink without alcohol.
I am not sure I need White Claw branding if there is no alcohol.
I would rather drink sparkling water.

first-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Then the name still means something to you even without the alcohol.

first-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Fair. You are mostly deciding whether you still want the White Claw part when the alcohol is gone.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That sounds like a branding case study.

first-2-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Please never say that at the beach.

first-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Sparkling water remains extremely difficult to beat on simplicity.
The player already knows White Claw and sees ClawTails, a line built around recognizable cocktail flavor names.

entry-return-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Margarita. Cosmo. Mojito. Daiquiri.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You stole the cocktail menu.

entry-return-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Borrowed the names. Very different legal energy.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: And the can is not pretending to be the actual cocktail?

entry-return-5.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Cocktail-inspired flavors. Familiar cue, different product.

choice-return.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: That sounds fun for a rooftop hang.
Cocktail names are doing a lot of expectation-setting.
I would rather have the actual cocktail or the regular seltzer.

return-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Then the borrowed ritual makes the new line easy to understand.

return-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Exactly. Familiar names do some of the selling before taste does.

return-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Then the extension did not solve a problem for you.
